positions.as_written: Repair technique developed around the vascular boundary rather than around the tear pattern alone.
Read a contact pressure figure for its direction and treat its absolute value as method dependent.
Check what population a meniscectomy trial recruited before applying it, and say so when quoting it.
Read the root and extrusion literature as one subject, since a root tear that does not extrude and an extrusion without a root tear behave differently.
Do not look for a safe resection threshold in this literature, because the relationship it describes is continuous.
Weigh the patient's age and physiology, because the pressure argument has forty years to act in a thirty year old and ten in a seventy year old.
Weigh comorbidities, since several of them change both the anaesthetic risk and the rehabilitation.
Weigh the demands on the knee, because a locked knee in a roofer and a clicking knee in a swimmer are different problems.
Weigh their psychological state, since a patient convinced the knee is damaged beyond use will not rehabilitate it.
And elicit their ideas, concerns and expectations directly, because the commonest expectation brought to this consultation is that a scan finding must be fixed.
State the balance to the patient in those terms and record which way it fell.
Read Fairbank's observation and the modern trials together, because the second is the first with a control group.
